question: Does observed start-matched scoring improve actual online curriculum learning at matched process CPU?
tuning: No new tuning; same fixed original lr=.001 configuration in every arm, selected using prior studies. Prior outcomes known.
primary: Seed-group mean over both families: startmatched minus random intended-goal lower95% t bound >=.05; startmatched IID lower95% bound >=.80; startmatched minus DR IID lower95% bound >=-.05. All required. Other contrasts descriptive.
unit: 8 independent seed groups, averaging two family fits; within-group geometries shared across arms. No fixed-output episode pseudo-replication.
scope: Local adapter exposes same opaque start-identity access to all arms; only startmatched uses it. References contain observed returns only; first observation of an unseen start yields zero deficit, no complete optimal warm-up. Does not implement paper-exact ACCEL.
budget: 120 process CPU seconds, including scoring/ranking/environment steps, checked at complete PPO rollout boundaries. Actual overshoot retained; no claiming exact equal FLOPs. Evaluation and immutable snapshot serialization excluded. All total interactions, learning/scoring steps and compute recorded.
calibration: 15-CPU-second runs assess engineering/runtime only, disjoint streams. No confirmation outcome used for design or tuning. Small n limits precision; no guaranteed power.
frozen_result_rule: No exclusions, optional N extension, tuning or budget expansion after confirmation. Larger-budget conclusions remain untested.
